html:
The Partition of India was the division of British India into two independent states, India and Pakistan, at midnight on 14 to 15 August 1947. It ended the British Raj and set off one of the largest and bloodiest mass migrations in history.

The Congress under Nehru and Gandhi wanted one India. The Muslim League under Jinnah demanded a separate homeland for Muslims, and riots from 1946 made a deal impossible. Britain, exhausted by the war, brought its exit forward to August 1947.

The two Muslim-majority provinces at either end, Punjab and Bengal, were cut in two. A British lawyer who had never been to India drew the Radcliffe Line in five weeks, and the border was published only after independence. Everything else was divided too: the army, the railways, the civil service, the treasury. Over 500 princely states had to join one side or the other.

What followed:

  • About 15 million people crossed the new borders, Hindus and Sikhs east, Muslims west.
  • Somewhere between a few hundred thousand and two million were killed in massacres, many on trains and roads.
  • Tens of thousands of women were abducted.
  • Kashmir's ruler joined India, and the two states went to war over it within weeks.

Pakistan's eastern wing later broke away in the 1971 war. Partition still shapes family memory, politics and relations between India and Pakistan.
sum: The Partition of India was the division of British India into two independent states, India and Pakistan, at midnight on 14 to 15 August 1947. It ended the British Raj and set off one of the largest and bloodiest mass migrations in history.
